newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks advance on second-quarter reports, bond drops.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks advance on second-quarter reports, bond drops.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed with solid gains Tuesday after strong earnings reports and sagging U.S. Treasury bond yields lured buyers into the market, analysts said.

"Second-quarter earnings have been good on the whole, with some contrasting cases. ... A good sign is they reflect a recovery in the domestic market and in purchasing power, as in retailers," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst with the Bursametrica consulting firm.
The leading IPC share index closed up 85.31 points, or 1.81 percent, at 4,797.49.

Cifra S.A.'s B shares were in demand after the retailer posted sharply higher earnings late Monday, dealers said. The stock climbed 56 centavos (7 cents) to close at 15.56 pesos ($2.00) in brisk trade.
Galvan said expected cuts in domestic primary rates later Tuesday were a boon to share prices, especially with the yield on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond close to its year low at 6.38 percent.
"Long-bond yields are rock-bottom ... and the bolsa (stock market) is getting more and more competitive compared with the money market," he said.

Nine money market traders surveyed by Reuters predicted Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Mexican treasury bond rates at an average of 18.01 percent, or .71 percentage point less than last week's auction.

Traders said the IPC, after reaching as high as 4,799.90 points, eased amid light profit-taking, specially notable on market heavyweight Cemex S.A. The cement maker shed 5 centavos (less than 1 cent) to close at 37.80 pesos ($4.86).
Volume picked up from a sluggish start to total a healthy 124.7 million shares traded.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced sliders by 64 to 44, out of 120 stocks traded in total.
